title: Minimum Swaps to Form Chessboard
description:
You are given an `n x n` binary grid `board`. In each move, you can swap any two rows with each other, or swap any two columns with each other.

Return the **minimum number of moves** required to transform `board` into a valid **chessboard**—a board where no two horizontally or vertically adjacent cells have the same value (`0` or `1`). If it is impossible to transform `board` into a chessboard, return `-1`.
hints: Row and column swaps preserve the rectangle parity invariant: for every (r, c), board[0][0] ^ board[r][0] ^ board[0][c] ^ board[r][c] must equal 0 (meaning every row equals row 0 or its bitwise complement).
Verify that both the first row and first column have either floor(n/2) or ceil(n/2) ones; then count misaligned rows and columns independently to find the minimum swaps.

examples.explanation: Swap columns 0 and 1, then swap rows 1 and 2 to obtain a valid 4x4 chessboard in 2 moves.
The 2x2 board is already a valid chessboard, requiring 0 moves.
Row 0 has [1,0] while row 1 has [1,1], which violates the complement invariant, so no chessboard is possible (-1).
